info.name: CineBook - Full Flow
info.description: Movie ticket booking microservices system. Everything routes through the API Gateway on :8080. Run the 'Full Flow (in order)' folder top-to-bottom with the Collection Runner for a complete register -> book -> pay -> notify pass -- each request auto-saves the IDs the next one needs into collection variables. Prerequisite: service-registry, config-server, api-gateway, and all 6 business services must be UP (check http://localhost:8761), and docker compose (6x MySQL + RabbitMQ) must be running. A default admin account (username 'admin', password 'Admin123!') is seeded automatically on user-service startup. AUTHORIZATION MODEL: browsing (GET movies/theaters/screens/seats/seat-categories) needs no token; creating/editing/deleting catalog data (theaters, screens, seat categories, movies, showtimes, cast) requires an ADMIN token; creating a booking and reading bookings/payments/notifications requires being logged in as any user (they carry personal data).

item.name: FULL FLOW (run in order)

request.description: Creates a CUSTOMER account. Change the username/email if you re-run this -- they're unique.
Re-authenticates and refreshes the token (proves the login path independently of register).
Confirms the JWT from step 1/2 is accepted by user-service's Spring Security filter. Uses {{token}} (the collection's default bearer auth).

Catalog management (theaters/screens/seats/movies/showtimes) requires ROLE_ADMIN. user-service seeds one default admin on startup: username 'admin', password 'Admin123!'. Stored separately as {{adminToken}} so it doesn't overwrite your customer {{token}} from steps 1-2 -- you'll switch back to being 'the customer' again at step 11 (Create Booking).
Requires ROLE_ADMIN -- uses {{adminToken}} from step 4.
5 rows x 8 seats/row = 40-seat screen. Requires ROLE_ADMIN.

One-time seat-grid generation for the screen. categoryCode must match a seeded SeatCategory (theater-service seeds SILVER/GOLD/PREMIUM on startup via DataInitializer). Calling this twice for the same screen returns 400 (InvalidOperationException). Requires ROLE_ADMIN.
genres are resolved-or-created by name -- no need to create Genre rows separately. Requires ROLE_ADMIN.

body.raw: {"title": "Test Movie", "description": "A movie created for Postman testing", "durationMinutes": 120, "language": "English", "releaseDate": "2026-01-01", "rating": 8.5, "posterUrl": "https://example.com/poster.jpg", "genres": ["Action", "Drama"]}

request.description: price here is the actual per-ticket price booking-service will charge -- Movie itself has no top-level price, only its showtimes do. Requires ROLE_ADMIN.
Public read, no token needed -- this is what booking-service's Feign client calls internally to price a booking.

Back to being the customer -- uses {{token}} (the collection default), not {{adminToken}}. booking-service looks up the showtime via Feign (movie-service), then the movie/theater/screen, computes amount = showtime.price * seatCount, saves the booking, and publishes booking.confirmed to RabbitMQ. seatCount must not exceed the screen's capacity (totalRows x seatsPerRow = 40 here). Requires being logged in as any user -- a booking always belongs to someone.

ASYNC: payment-service consumes booking.confirmed off RabbitMQ and creates this payment (auto COMPLETED, no real gateway). If you get 404 immediately after step 11, wait a second and resend -- message processing isn't instant. Use Collection Runner's delay, or just click Send again. Requires being logged in (contains personal data) -- uses {{token}}.

ASYNC: notification-service consumes payment.completed off RabbitMQ and logs+persists a simulated email (no real provider wired up). Same retry note as step 12. Requires being logged in -- uses {{token}}.

item.description: Run this whole folder with the Collection Runner for one full pass: register (customer) -> login -> admin login -> build a theater/screen/seats -> build a movie/showtime (all as admin) -> book as the customer again -> auto-pay -> auto-notify. Each request saves what the next one needs, so you can also just click through them top to bottom by hand.
